source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Theories of Growth and Development
questions.stem: At a well-child visit, which skill does the nurse expect a 2-year-old to perform?
questions.rationale: Two-year-olds kick a ball; tricycle and scissors at 3 years; shoelaces about 5 years.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 164)
questions.quote: A 2-year-old usually can kick a ball fonvard.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Theories of Growth and Development
questions.stem: A 5-year-old screams that all his blood will come out if the bandage is removed after a blood test. This reflects fear of:
questions.rationale: Preschoolers fear body mutilation and view procedures as invasions that damage the body.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 164)
questions.quote: The child does not understand that exsanguination will not occur from an injection site.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: The best way for parents to handle a toddler's temper tantrum is to:
options: Ignore it while keeping the child safe
Pick the child up at once
Reason with the child during it
Give a treat to stop it
questions.rationale: Ignoring tantrums (if safe) avoids reinforcing them; they reflect the toddler's drive for autonomy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 164)
questions.quote: Children who have temper tantrums should be ignored as long as they are safe.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which food is best for a child at home after tonsillectomy?
questions.rationale: Soft, cool foods and liquids are tolerated; avoid hard, scratchy foods until the throat heals.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 164)
questions.quote: For the first few days after a T and A, liquids and soft foods are best tolerated by the child while the throat is sore.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The diet recommended for a child with cystic fibrosis is:
questions.rationale: Pancreatic insufficiency causes malabsorption; children need high-calorie, high-protein diets with enzymes.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 164)
questions.quote: a moderate fat, hi - rotein;hi -calorie diet is indicated.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A toddler with tetralogy of Fallot turns blue and breathes fast while crying. The nurse first:
options: Places the child in knee-chest position
Tells the child it will be quick
questions.rationale: Knee-chest position increases systemic resistance and reduces right-to-left shunting during a "tet spell."
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 165)
questions.quote: The child is experiencing a 'ftet spell" or hypoxic episode. Therefore the nurse should place the child in a knee-to-chest position.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: To ease painful joints in a child with rheumatic fever, the nurse uses:
questions.rationale: Joints are so tender that even bed linens hurt; a bed cradle keeps linens off them.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 165)
questions.quote: Use of a bed cradle is recommended to help remove the weight of the linens on painful joints.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The priority nursing diagnosis for a newborn with tracheoesophageal fistula is risk for:
questions.rationale: The blind pouch fills with fluid and secretions, so aspiration pneumonia is the major risk.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 166)
questions.quote: Because the blind pouch associated with TEF fills quickly xsith fluids, the child is at high risk for aspiration.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After repair of an imperforate anus, the infant is positioned:
options: On the side with hips elevated
questions.rationale: Side-lying with hips elevated (or supine with legs suspended) avoids pressure and tension on the perineum.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 166)
questions.quote: on cither side with the hips elevated to prevent pressure on the perineum.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child swallowed a large amount of paracetamol. The antidote the nurse prepares is:
questions.rationale: Acetylcysteine prevents liver damage; watch for right upper quadrant pain from hepatotoxicity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 170)
questions.quote: Acetylcysteine prevents hepatotoxicity caused by acetaminophen poisoning.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: An adolescent had surgery for an undescended testis as a child. The most important teaching is:
questions.rationale: Testicular cancer risk is higher after undescended testes, so monthly self-examination is taught.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: it is extremely Important to teach the adoQent how to perform the testicular self.examination monthly.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: For a child with acute glomerulonephritis with edema and low urine output, the most important assessment is:
questions.rationale: Weight is the best indicator of fluid balance.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: Because weight is the best indicator of fluid balance, obtaining daily weights would be the highest priority.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has a suspected Wilms' tumor. The nurse must avoid:
questions.rationale: Abdominal palpation may rupture the encapsulated tumor and spread cancer cells; post a sign.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: Ihe abdomen of the child with Wilm•s tumor should not be palpated because of the danger of disseminating tumor cells.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Before surgery, a newborn with an unrepaired myelomeningocele is positioned:
options: On the back with hips flexed
questions.rationale: Prone positioning keeps pressure off the sac and allows good hip alignment.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: Before surgery. the infant is kept in the prone position to decrease tension on the sac.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Immediately after insertion of a VP shunt on the right side of the head, the child is positioned:
questions.rationale: Keep flat at first to avoid rapid CSF drainage and subdural hematoma; avoid lying on the shunt valve.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: the child is positioned supine with the head of the bed flat to prevent too rapid decrease in CSF pressure.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An appropriate goal for a child with Down syndrome is to:
questions.rationale: The goal is maximum independence; consistent limits and repetition are needed.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: goal in working with mentally challenged children is to train them to be as independent as possible.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An adolescent taking valproic acid should report:
questions.rationale: Valproic acid can cause liver toxicity; jaundice must be reported promptly.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: A toxic effect of valproic acid (Depakene) is liver toxicity, which may manifest Voith jaundice

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A hospitalized preschooler is angry that his discharge was delayed. The best play activity is:
questions.rationale: Physical activity gives a safe outlet for anger; fine-motor tasks may add frustration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: Pounding on a pegboard offers the opportunity.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Parents of a child who nearly drowned say they feel guilty. The best response is:
options: "Tell me more about your feelings of guilt."
"Don't feel guilty; he will be fine."
questions.rationale: Open-ended, nonjudgmental responses let parents express guilt; blaming and false reassurance block communication.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: The parents need to be allowed to express their feelings openly in a nonthreatening, nonjudgmental atmosphere.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Teaching for parents of an infant in a Pavlik harness includes:
options: Fit the diaper under the straps
Powder the skin under the straps
questions.rationale: The harness is worn continuously over a diaper; check skin several times daily and avoid powders and lotions.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: The Pavlik harness is wom over a diaper.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother of a boy with Duchenne muscular dystrophy shows understanding when she says:
options: "He'll likely lose walking ability by about 9 to 11."
questions.rationale: Duchenne is progressive X-linked; affected boys usually cannot walk independently by 9–11 years.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 169)
questions.quote: Children who are affected by this disease usually are unable to independently by age 9-11 years.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 9-month-old with severe diarrhea has metabolic acidosis. The nurse expects:
questions.rationale: The lungs compensate for metabolic acidosis by increasing ventilation (tachypnea, deep breaths).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 169)
questions.quote: The body compensates for metabolic acidosis through the lungs which try to eliminate the buffered acids by increasing alveolar ventilation

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Theories of Growth and Development
questions.stem: A 4-year-old wants to finish his board game before his dressing is changed. This reflects Erikson's stage of:
questions.rationale: Preschoolers in initiative vs. guilt feel accomplishment in completing activities they start.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 169)
questions.quote: A child who v,ants to finish his game of candyland before his dressing is changed is in the stage of initiative.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding best shows that a 3-year-old after surgery is no longer in pain?
questions.rationale: A pain-free child resumes play; tachycardia and poor appetite suggest ongoing pain.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 169)
questions.quote: A child who is pain-free likes to play.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant has repeated middle-ear infections. The most important question for the mother is whether:
questions.rationale: Stopping antibiotics early leads to recurrence, hearing loss or systemic infection.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 170)
questions.quote: If the client is not receiving her full course of antibiotic therapy her ear infections "ill recur

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Theories of Growth and Development
questions.stem: The anterior fontanel normally closes by:
questions.rationale: The anterior fontanel closes at 12–18 months; the posterior by about 2–3 months.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 170)
questions.quote: It nonnally closes between ages 12 and 1 8 months.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Theories of Growth and Development
questions.stem: Which developmental change is typical of adolescence?
questions.rationale: Adolescents develop abstract thinking and secondary sex characteristics and often take risks.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 170)
questions.quote: During adolescence, abstract thinking and secondary sex characteristics are developed and high-risk behaviors are common.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Child Care: Legal, Collaboration & Teamwork
questions.stem: Which child should raise the nurse's suspicion of abuse?
options: A shy 2-year-old who avoids eye contact
questions.rationale: Bruises on protected areas like the back plus withdrawal are red flags; shin bruises are common in toddlers.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 171)
questions.quote: A 3-year old child who acts withdrawn and has bruises on his back may be the victim of child abuse.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A typical finding in a child with immune thrombocytopenic purpura is:
questions.rationale: ITP causes petechiae, easy bruising and mucosal bleeding from low platelets.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pediatric exercises (PDF p. 171)
questions.quote: The common symptoms of idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura include easy bruising, petechiae, and bleeding from mucous membranes.
